phase: PHASE-03 - GPWCF Framework Filesystem & Package Architecture
purpose: Accepted filesystem/package ownership architecture for the GPWCF source and verification skeleton. The physical tree materializes only approved package boundaries and package markers; unresolved contracts do not become placeholder modules or public APIs.

scope.referenceConsumerRole: Reference consumer used to test framework genericity only. Its 13 stages, stage models, step models, tools and business policies do not determine GPWCF folder names or package structure.
exclusions: No specialized Stage, Step, SPU or Supporting Pattern contract is modified.
No Generator stage/step model or Generator-specific contract is copied into GPWCF.
No generic Pipeline Root entity/package is created.
No Prefect adoption reconsideration; Prefect 3.9.2 remains accepted.
Draft Wave 1-6 detailed designs are not implementation authority until explicitly accepted.

designPrinciples: Allocate directories by cohesive ownership and dependency boundary, not by source document names, contract filenames or consumer workflow stage numbering.
Stage, Step and SPU are distinct Entities. Their packages are the organizing centers for the contracts and components that realize their responsibilities.

Composition is owned by the Aggregate it composes: Stage Composition is nested under Stage; Step Composition is nested under Step. Composition is not a peer top-level entity or generic framework package.

A component belongs with the Entity/Aggregate that owns its invocation, coordination and result semantics unless it is independently reusable with its own specialized contract, in which case it receives its own package.
SPU is an independently callable processing Entity, not a Step subfolder.
Supporting Patterns are independent optional capability packages. They are not subclasses or instances of an assumed universal SupportingUnit base.
Public API is an explicit curated stable boundary under public_api; __init__.py files alone do not define the public contract.
Core and Prefect Integration have separate import and dependency boundaries. Core must remain usable with Prefect absent.
Only create directories for established responsibilities. Do not create speculative managers, registries, universal adapters, shared-contracts packages or empty component taxonomies.
Keep development documentation, PoC evidence and runtime source separate.
The filesystem represents semantic ownership and allowed dependencies; it does not imply that every contract document is an implemented Python type.

Include the project license when distribution is prepared; do not invent license content.
Minimal namespace/package initialization. Must not eagerly import Core internals, optional patterns or Prefect.
Minimal Core package marker; does not eagerly import entities, optional patterns or Prefect.
Prefect-independent domain entities, contracts, composition ownership and typed results.
Prefect-specific functional binding, native hierarchy invocation and operational mapping; isolated from Core.
Core contract, entity, composition and result tests in a Prefect-free environment.
Public import, export, compatibility and API boundary tests.
Prefect binding and operational mapping tests, clearly distinguishing fixture qualification from production GPWCF binding.
Dependency direction, forbidden-import, optional-pattern isolation and package boundary checks.
Consumer-facing documentation only. Governing architecture decision records remain under .docs.
Retain PHASE-01/02 evidence and PHASE-03 architecture artifacts here; do not relocate them as part of source package creation.
Retain Prefect qualification scripts, evidence and local PoC assets outside distributable runtime packages.
Keep current solution-level aggregation semantics; it is not the authoritative published Core runtime dependency manifest.

entityAndCompositionPlacement.rule: The Entity/Aggregate is the directory ownership center. Its Composition is a child package of that Entity's package.

placements.relationship: Composition nested within owning Stage Aggregate; coordinates Step public contracts.
Composition nested within owning Step Aggregate; coordinates SPUs and selected Supporting Unit contracts.
Standalone callable processing entity; composed by Step but not owned by Step.
Independent optional capability package; selected and coordinated by Step Composition through its specialized contract.

entityAndCompositionPlacement.componentPlacementRule: Do not create core/components as a peer root. Internal components are placed under the owning Entity/Aggregate when their function is aggregate-owned. Independently reusable executable entities receive their own domain package. A future components/ subpackage is allowed only when multiple established cohesive components exist and the boundary is justified.

publicApiAndImportRules: Only modules below src/gpwcf/public_api are supported consumer import paths.
Internal modules below src/gpwcf/core and src/gpwcf/integrations are implementation locations, not stable consumer API.
Core API import must succeed when Prefect is not installed.
Core package initialization must not eagerly import optional Supporting Patterns.
Step Composition may import only the selected Supporting Pattern contract surfaces; no import of every optional pattern is allowed.
Supporting Pattern packages must not import Step Composition implementation.
Prefect Integration depends inward on Core Public API and must not depend on Core private modules.
Core must never import integrations.prefect, Prefect types, Prefect State or Prefect runtime packages.
Consumer code must not import GPWCF private modules or use Prefect Integration implementation internals.
No wildcard exports that silently enlarge the stable API surface.
No circular runtime imports between Entity Aggregates; use contract/protocol boundaries and type-only references where necessary.
The conceptual public API boundary is accepted, but source public_api package markers and exports remain deferred until Wave 6 Public API design acceptance.

dependencyManifestPlacement.existingSolutionRoot: SMRB solution-root .dependencies/ is the location for external dependency/source assets and project-scoped dependency material. SMRB solution-root .env/ is the shared Python virtual environment. Both remain solution-level and outside the GPWCF repository.
dependencyManifestPlacement.gpwcfRoot: Do not create GPWCF/.dependencies, a duplicate venv, embedded Python runtime, or copied dependency bundle. Use the existing sibling solution-root SMRB/.dependencies/ hierarchy for external dependency assets and SMRB/.env/ for the shared developer interpreter.
dependencyManifestPlacement.coreRuntime: No third-party runtime dependencies in current baseline; Python standard library only.
dependencyManifestPlacement.prefectIntegration: Prefect 3.9.2 belongs to the optional Integration installation profile. The exact transitive closure and lock must be derived from a clean isolated environment before release.
dependencyManifestPlacement.generator: pygccxml and Generator extraction/tool dependencies remain in the Generator consumer's own requirements.
dependencyManifestPlacement.pyprojectPolicy: The eventual root pyproject.toml describes the single distribution and optional prefect extra. Do not create build metadata until the build backend and build-system requirements are selected and pinned.
dependencyManifestPlacement.lockPolicy: Do not check in the 106-package environment snapshot as the minimal lock. Keep qualification environment snapshots under PHASE-00/PoC evidence; add a minimized Integration lock only after clean resolution and verification.
dependencyManifestPlacement.buildBackend: Build backend and build-system requirements are development/build dependencies, not Core runtime requirements; select and pin them as a separate packaging decision.
dependencyManifestPlacement.distributionDecision: Accepted initial packaging shape: one distribution with a dependency-free Core base and optional prefect extra. Build backend and build-system pinning remain deferred until FS-GATE-02 is closed.
dependencyManifestPlacement.pythonProjectAssets: The user-designated Python project dependency asset location is the SMRB solution-root .dependencies/ hierarchy, with project-scoped assets under .dependencies/SMRB.GenericPipelineWorkflowComponentsFramework/. The shared interpreter remains SMRB/.env/.
dependencyManifestPlacement.draftPackagingProposal: The draft Packaging design proposes setuptools.build_meta with setuptools==84.2.1, gpwcf 0.1.0, Python >=3.15,<3.16, optional prefect extra and py.typed. These details are not adopted by this PHASE-03 skeleton; pyproject.toml and py.typed remain deferred pending Wave 6 acceptance.

acceptance: Run Core tests in a clean environment with Prefect and Generator dependencies absent.
Verify import of gpwcf.public_api.core does not load Prefect modules.
Verify each optional pattern can be imported independently and unselected patterns are not required.
Verify Integration imports only when the Prefect optional installation profile is active.
Verify forbidden dependency edges and circular imports.
Verify public imports resolve only documented symbols and internal modules are not relied on by consumer tests.
Test Stage-to-Step and Step-to-SPU boundaries without allowing Stage-to-SPU direct invocation.
Keep fixture-level Prefect qualification tests distinct from production GPWCF binding tests.

documentationPlacement.rule: Architecture decision records and qualification evidence remain outside distributable source packages; consumer-facing usage documentation may be published under docs/.

excludedFilesystemConcepts.reason: No generic GPWCF Pipeline Root Entity or contract is established.
No cohesive generic shared contract module has been demonstrated; do not create a folder solely because terms are shared.
Components are allocated to their owning Entity/Aggregate; no independent cross-entity components root is justified.
Composition belongs to Stage or Step Aggregate and must not be elevated into a universal peer package.
No universal SupportingUnit base contract is established.
GPWCF does not own scheduler, dispatch engine, worker manager or runtime orchestrator.
No universal plugin manager, dynamic loader or runtime registry is part of the accepted architecture.
Generator Common Error Model dependency closure and genericity are unresolved; keep current model consumer-owned.
No universal adapter layer; Prefect-specific binding belongs only in integrations/prefect.
Shared SMRB .dependencies/.env already owns solution-level development dependency setup.
Generator is a consumer, not a GPWCF subpackage.

acceptanceCriteria: Filesystem is organized around Stage, Step and SPU Entities and their ownership boundaries, not around Generator stages or contract document filenames.
Stage Composition is nested within Stage Aggregate; Step Composition is nested within Step Aggregate.
SPU remains an independent processing entity invoked by Step Composition.
Supporting Patterns remain independent optional capability packages with no universal base assumption.
Core and Prefect Integration source and Public API boundaries are distinct.
Core imports and installs without Prefect; Prefect imports remain isolated to opt-in Integration.
Public API is an explicit curated contract boundary; internal implementation paths are not supported consumer imports.
No generic Pipeline Root, shared_contracts, universal components/composition package, runtime orchestrator, adapter framework, plugin manager or universal SupportingUnit base is introduced.
No GPWCF-local dependency directory or Python runtime bundle is created.
Generator remains an external reference consumer and its dependencies/contracts remain outside GPWCF.
PoC evidence and architecture records remain outside distributable runtime package.
All unresolved contract and packaging decisions remain explicit and are not silently decided by folder layout.
MOD-CORE-STEP-RESULTS is explicitly mapped to src/gpwcf/core/step/results/ as a distinct logical module nested within Step.
No src/gpwcf/core/stage/results/, src/gpwcf/core/step/error_model/, src/gpwcf/core/shared_contracts/, or speculative Stage Prefect binding/public facade file is materialized.
The initial distribution shape is one distribution with an optional prefect extra; pyproject build metadata waits for build-backend selection.
The solution-root SMRB/.dependencies/ store and SMRB/.env/ shared interpreter are reused without creating GPWCF-local duplicates.
The public API test path mirrors gpwcf.public_api.integrations.prefect as tests/public_api/integrations/prefect/.
All 16 detailed design-wave proposals remain explicitly pending and none of their proposed modules or public API files is materialized by this skeleton.
The conceptual Public API boundary is retained, but src/gpwcf/public_api/ is absent until Wave 6 Public API design acceptance.
